result.summary:
STANDARD TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR CHECKS: ALL PASS. Read test/specs/REQ-203.md (14-item AC mapping) and test/letflow/repository/activation_test.exs (28 tests) in full. Every one of REQ-203's 12 ACs has real, non-vacuous coverage -- verified directly, not by trusting TEST-DESIGNER's own mapping. Specifically inspected AC1/AC2's concurrency test: it genuinely uses Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) plus a Task.async'd activate_group/4 call paused via test_pause_after: 1/test_pause_fun, with the main test process issuing REAL resolve/3 reads from a separate connection during the pause and asserting ALL THREE artifacts show OLD versions (including artifact 1, whose row is already internally updated but uncommitted) -- this is a real test of Postgres's MVCC visibility floor per design §4.3, not a vacuous commit-then-read check. No @tag :skip, no 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in either file (grepped directly). Fixtures (provisioned_tenant!/insert_tenant!/drop_schema!) are self-contained, matching test/letflow/repository_test.exs's shape without importing/sharing it (DIRECTIVE T-4) -- confirmed by reading the fixture code, not by trusting the claim. No hardcoded secrets/connection strings. Ran mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors myself: clean, no output, exit 0. Ran mix test test/letflow/repository_test.exs test/letflow/repository/canonicaliser_test.exs myself: 39/39 passed, confirming the seam is behavior-preserving for REQ-202's own suite. Ran mix test test/letflow/repository/activation_test.exs myself: 28/28 passed.

AC8 MUTATION CLAIM -- INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST: applied my own mutant to resolve/3 (lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex) -- when no artifact_activations row exists, fall back to the latest artifact_versions row by version_number instead of returning {:error, :not_activated}. Ran test/letflow/repository/activation_test.exs against the mutant: 26/28 passed, 2 FAILED -- exactly 'AC8 ... resolve/3 returns {:error, :not_activated} when no activation row exists' and 'AC3 -- per-tenant isolation ... activating in tenant A does not change tenant B's active version', matching TEST-DESIGNER's own reported counts exactly. Reverted with `git checkout -- lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex`; verified the revert with `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` (empty output) AND re-ran the suite (28/28 passed again). This mutant-isolation-and-revert cycle was performed by me, not copied from TEST-DESIGNER's report.

DECISION 1 -- THE TEST-ONLY SEAM ON activate_group/4: ROUTING TO REVIEWER REQUIRED. I read the actual diff (git show 4d6ba4ee -- lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex) myself rather than trusting TEST-DESIGNER's characterization. The change is genuinely additive and behavior-preserving for every existing call site: arity 4 -> 5 with opts \\ [] (old 4-arg calls unaffected), a private maybe_add_test_pause_step/3 helper that is a structural no-op unless both test_pause_after and test_pause_fun are supplied (pattern-matches pause_after against the loop index; when opts is [], pause_after is nil and can never equal an integer index, so the clause never fires), and I confirmed this empirically with my own regression run (39/39, not just re-reading TEST-DESIGNER's claim). However, I am deciding this needs a fresh REVIEWER pass before TEST-RUNNER, for reasons that go beyond 'is it behavior-preserving': (1) This is new production-file surface (a changed public arity, a new @type) added to lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex AFTER REVIEWER's Step 2d PASS -- REVIEWER has never seen this exact code. CLAUDE.md's central redundancy principle ('every producing step has a validating step... this is the project's central redundancy principle, adopted specifically so the pipeline stays reliable even when the executing model is weak') does not carve out an exception for changes a later agent judges safe -- the point of the principle is that no single agent's own judgment substitutes for the designated gate, however careful that agent's own verification was. I am TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, not REVIEWER; confirming the diff is behavior-preserving is within my mandate, but signing off on its OTP-idiom/security soundness is REVIEWER's designated authority, not mine. (2) There is a real, non-formality idiom/security question here that only REVIEWER is positioned to rule on: a synchronous, caller-supplied 0-arity closure (test_pause_fun) is now invoked from inside an open Ecto.Multi transaction. Nothing in Elixir's type system prevents a future non-test caller from discovering and passing test_pause_after/test_pause_fun in production (the option is a private-helper concern, not a compile-time-enforced restriction) -- e.g. a caller holding a DB transaction open indefinitely via a hung callback, which would tie up a connection-pool slot. This is exactly the class of 'looks safe in isolation but is a latent backdoor shape' judgment call REVIEWER's OTP-idiom/supervision-integrity mandate exists for, and it did not exist in the code REVIEWER already passed. (3) Design §4.3 anticipated this exact mechanism's necessity ('a Multi.run/3 step that blocks on a message/Agent signal'), which means this is a design-anticipated gap that fell through Step 2a (ELIXIR-DEV should have built it, or CODE-DESIGNER should have flagged it as a required production surface, not a test-time addition) -- this is a legitimate, foreseeable omission, not an exotic edge case, and REVIEWER should have the chance to say whether ELIXIR-DEV (not TEST-DESIGNER) should own this addition.

DECISION 2 -- THE @spec-vs-BEHAVIOR MISMATCH: ROUTING TO ELIXIR-DEV REQUIRED, same class of defect this session's own REQ-202 REVIEWER already treated as BLOCKING. Checked: no acceptance criterion in REQ-203's 12 ACs requires the graceful {:error, {atom(), Changeset.t()}} tuple specifically -- AC1's actual wording is 'atomic multi-artifact activation, all-succeed and forced-failure-rollback (no partial state, no history rows)', which the raised-exception path still satisfies (the transaction rolls back correctly either way, confirmed by TEST-DESIGNER's test and re-confirmed by my own reading of it). But I checked this session's own precedent directly (handoffs/WF02-REQ202-20260830/step-02d-reviewer.json) rather than accepting TEST-DESIGNER's 'minor -- atomicity unaffected' self-classification at face value: REQ-202's REVIEWER blocked Step 2a specifically because 'a wrong/incomplete @spec is exactly the kind of documented-contract-vs-actual-behavior mismatch that produces an unhandled-case crash at a caller who pattern-matches exhaustively against what the spec says is possible' -- and explicitly rejected the framing that this is a stylistic nitpick. REQ-203's activate_group/4 has the identical defect shape: its own @spec (lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex) advertises {:error, {atom(), Ecto.Changeset.t()}} for a mid-transaction failure, but a real FK violation (confirmed live against Postgres by TEST-DESIGNER, and structurally confirmed by me reading upsert_activation_pointer/8's repo.update call, which has no foreign_key_constraint/3 mapped on the Activation changeset) raises Ecto.ConstraintError instead. Any future caller (a controller, another context module) that pattern-matches exhaustively against activate_group/4's documented error union -- exactly the failure mode REQ-202's REVIEWER named -- gets an unhandled crash. This is materially different from an 'unreachable-in-practice caller-error path': a stale or cross-tenant version_id is a plausible real caller mistake, not a theoretical one, and the whole reason TEST-DESIGNER caught it was by exercising the real failure path (not by inspection). Treating this defect differently here than REQ-202 did in the same session, for the same defect class, in the same file family, only two commits apart, would be an unprincipled inconsistency this project's own 'don't silently re-decide' discipline warns against by analogy. This is NOT acceptable to ship with a follow-up issue filed instead -- it needs ELIXIR-DEV's fix now, before TEST-RUNNER.

CONCLUSION: FAILED. Two rework routes are required, sequenced to avoid a redundant double REVIEWER pass:
1. ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a rework): add foreign_key_constraint/3 mapping(s) to the changeset used by upsert_activation_pointer/8's internal repo.update call in lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex, so a mid-Multi FK violation (bogus/foreign version_id) returns {:error, {atom(), Ecto.Changeset.t()}} as activate_group/4's own @spec already promises, instead of raising Ecto.ConstraintError. This is the ONLY fix needed at this step -- no design-document rework, matching REQ-202's own step-02d 'implementation-level @spec-accuracy defect, not a design gap' finding for the identical class of issue.
2. REVIEWER (Step 2d re-check, ONE combined pass covering BOTH): (a) the ELIXIR-DEV fix from item 1, and (b) the TEST-ONLY seam (activate_group/4 arity 4->5, test_pause_after/test_pause_fun, the maybe_add_test_pause_step/3 helper) that TEST-DESIGNER added at Step 3 and that REVIEWER has not yet seen -- specifically asked to confirm: is a synchronous test-only callback invoked inside an open Multi transaction an acceptable idiom in this codebase, and does leaving it reachable via a private opts keyword (rather than e.g. compile-time-stripped via Mix.env()) pose a real production risk worth mitigating.
3. TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3 rework, after 1+2 land): update the 'a version_id with no matching artifact_versions row rolls back the whole group' test in test/letflow/repository/activation_test.exs to assert the corrected {:error, {atom(), Ecto.Changeset.t()}} return instead of assert_raise Ecto.ConstraintError, and update test/specs/REQ-203.md's corresponding entry.
4. TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (me, Step 3b re-check): re-verify after 1-3 land.

All other coverage in this test suite is sound and does not need to be revisited by this rework loop -- routing back over these two specific findings only.
